hq.headline: HQ's Bracket: San Diego State Cuts the Nets, Texas Wins the West, and Utah St. Crashes the Final Four
hq.writeup:
Bracketology HQ has filed. Sixty-seven picks, no simulations, one champion, and a long list of people who will enjoy watching me be wrong.

THE CHAMPION
San Diego State. Yes, it's the No. 1 overall seed. No, I'm not sorry. The Aztecs are 32-1 with six top-25 wins and no bad losses, an average margin of 30.7 points, and a rating of 40.29, more than four points clear of Alabama and nearly eight clear of everyone else. People will tell you the Mountain West tournament exposed them: 65-64 over UNLV, then 76-75 in overtime over Utah St. I'd say it did the opposite. A team that wins by 49 in February and by one in the final has shown it can win both kinds of game. You need six wins in a row. They've done both kinds.

The final is San Diego State over Texas.

THE FINAL FOUR
East: San Diego State, past Kansas in the Elite Eight. Kansas has won seven straight and the Big 12 tournament, and it's the most likely team in the region to make this uncomfortable.

South: Alabama, past Iowa St. Seven top-25 wins, the SEC tournament title, and a semifinal 72-66 win over Texas. Iowa St. has played the toughest schedule of anyone on the top four lines and gets to the Elite Eight by knocking out Gonzaga. Alabama loses to San Diego State in the national semifinal, which is a game I'd pay real money to watch.

West: Texas. This is my hot take from the column, and I'm putting my bracket where my mouth is. Florida State is 33-1, but its schedule is rated 5.71, the softest of any 1 seed, and Texas is rated higher at 32.61 to 29.54 after playing a schedule rated 11.19. Texas beats Seton Hall in the Sweet 16 and Florida State in the Elite Eight.

Midwest: Utah St. The bold one. It's a 3 seed with the fifth-best rating in the country, 31.8, and it lost the Mountain West final to the No. 1 overall in overtime by one point. I have it beating Georgetown in the Sweet 16 and Florida in the Elite Eight. Florida is a deserving 1 seed with six top-25 wins. Utah St. is simply the better team on a neutral floor by rating, and the tournament is nothing but neutral floors.

THE UPSETS I PICKED
12 Tennessee St. over 5 Miami. Fifteen straight wins against three bad losses and a first-game exit to a 12-20 Boston College team. I'll take the streak.

11 West Virginia over 6 Iowa. Iowa went 3-7 in its last ten and lost its only Big 10 tournament game to Ohio St. West Virginia has two top-25 wins.

10 Colorado State over 7 Marquette. Thirteen straight wins before Utah St. stopped it, two top-25 wins, and a schedule rated 10.03.

10 New Mexico State over 7 Michigan. Michigan just lost the Big 10 final by 21. New Mexico State lost to Delaware, which is worse, but the ratings are nearly level at 17.34 to 17.6 and I want one revenge story in my bracket.

9 Duke over 8 BYU and 9 Purdue over 8 Wisconsin. Rated higher, and in Purdue's case it won the league.

THE UPSETS I RESISTED
12 Rutgers over 5 Texas Tech. Rutgers is the hottest team in the field, four wins in four days to take the Big 10. Texas Tech is rated 14th and Rutgers 53rd. Hot streaks are real until they meet a nine-point rating gap. Texas Tech, then out to North Carolina.

12 Navy over 5 VCU. Navy is 30-3 and deserves better than this draw. VCU has won 25 straight. One of them was always going home. VCU wins, then beats Kansas State before Florida ends the run in the Sweet 16.

12 Saint Peter's over 5 Vanderbilt. Close, and tempting. Saint Peter's has five bad losses, Vanderbilt three top-25 wins. Vanderbilt.

THE TOUGHEST REGION
The East. Its top four seeds add up to the highest combined rating in the bracket, and it has the No. 1 overall, a red-hot Kansas, Butler fresh off the Big East title, and Rutgers lurking at 12. San Diego State has earned an easier walk than this, and it isn't getting one.

THE FIRST FOUR
Bradley over Oklahoma State, Texas A&M over Michigan St., UC San Diego over High Point and Oakland over Wagner. Bradley went 28-5. Texas A&M was in my last four in all along, and I'm not letting go now.

That's the bracket. Beat it if you can. Most of you will, and I'll say so in the column when you do.
